title: StructuresFile
description: The JSON shape of one file in `data/structures/`.

$schema.description:
Optional: the JSON Schema this file follows, so editors can check
it as you type (`"$schema": "../schema/structures.schema.json"`).

Colour.description:
The colours a material can be drawn in. A short fixed list rather than
any colour at all, so every terminal can show them (decision D16).

oneOf.description: Doors, so they stand out from the walls around them.

climb.description:
A ladder, going `"up"` or `"down"`. Only for walkable structures.
Optional: not a ladder.

colour.description:
Optional: the colour to draw it in, instead of the usual colour for
what it is (a damaged door is red, though you walk through it).

description.description: A sentence or two for look mode.

glyph.description: The character the map draws it with.

id.description: How maps refer to it, like `"bulkhead"`.

leak_cm2.description:
A hole to space, in cm² (a hull crack is 4, a breach 400): the space
beside it leaks. Only for solid structures. Optional: none.

material.description: The id of the material it's made of, unless a map says otherwise.

name.description: How it's shown to the player, like "bulkhead".

see_through.description:
You can see through it, though it's solid, like a window. Only for
solid structures (walkable ones never block sight). Optional: solid
structures block sight.

walkable.description:
You can walk on it, and air fills it. Optional: left out, it's
solid and airtight, like a wall or a shut door.

Vertical.description:
Up or down between decks. Up is `z + 1`: higher decks have higher numbers.
In data files it's `"up"` or `"down"` (a ladder's `climb`).
